discovery: Theoretical prediction of the interaction of CMB photons with hot plasma and primordial acoustic oscillations: the Sunyaev-Zel'dovich effects

nominees.name: Rashid Sunyaev
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute for Astrophysics, Garching; Space Research Institute (IKI), Moscow; Institute for Advanced Study, Princeton

motivation: With Zel'dovich, Rashid Sunyaev worked out from first principles how the cosmic microwave background is shaped by matter. In 1970 they predicted the acoustic oscillations imprinted on CMB anisotropies, which Planck, ACT and SPT have now measured with exquisite precision as the backbone of precision cosmology. In 1969-72 they predicted the thermal and kinetic Sunyaev-Zel'dovich effects: Compton scattering of CMB photons by hot electrons and moving plasma. The thermal SZ effect is now observed in thousands of galaxy clusters, giving redshift-independent cluster catalogues that constrain the growth of structure, dark energy and neutrino masses. The kinetic effect, detected statistically, probes cosmic velocities and the missing baryons. His work on spectral distortions and recombination underpins how we interpret the CMB. These are clean, quantitative predictions confirmed by observation, and they remain central tools for Simons Observatory and CMB-S4. Zel'dovich has died, so Sunyaev is the sole living originator.
